gap: No result ChatGPT got states the California Energy Commission's lab-tested weighted efficiency for the US 120 V plug-in microinverters: APsystems EZ1-LV 95%, Hoymiles HMS-360/391/420-1WM-LV (HiFlow Pro LV) 95.5%, NEP BDM-1200-LV 96.5%, with no 120 V EcoFlow entry on the list.
standout_why: I opened four of the rival pages. Solar Waypoint (cited) says outright that it ran no hands-on tests and uses only published specs. The balconysolarkits.us tracker (cited) gives only output ratings and calls its 'Verified' labels primary-source reads, not lab data. pluginsolarcheck.com/kits/certifications (cited) covers certification status only, with no efficiency or standby figures. howtogosolar.org lists maker ratings for mostly EU or rooftop models and names no lab. None of them gives a measured or CEC-listed efficiency for any 120 V plug-in inverter. None mentions the CEC Solar Equipment List.
decides: It mostly confirms the EZ1-LV pick rather than changing it. The EZ1-LV is on California's grid-support list, where its 95% weighted efficiency is a point below the 96% peak on the APsystems datasheet. The Hoymiles HiFlow Pro LV sizes ChatGPT recommended are 0.5 point higher, but only the 360, 391 and 420 W models are listed, not the 450 or 500. ChatGPT's 'higher-output option to watch', the EcoFlow STREAM Microinverter, has no 120 V entry on the list. NEP's BDM-1200-LV, which turned up in ChatGPT's results but was never recommended, lists 1.2 kW at 96.5%, the highest of the plug-in-class 120 V microinverters. The gaps are small: 1.5 points is about 15 kWh a year per 1,000 kWh of DC input. So the finding mainly tells shoppers which inverters a US state lab list covers, rather than ranking them by efficiency.

findings.label: CEC weighted efficiency
findings.source_title: Grid Support Solar Inverters - Solar Equipment List - California Energy Commission
findings.note: Row 'EZ1-LV {120V}', manufacturer Altenergy Power System Inc. (APsystems): 900 VA, 120 Vac grid-support microinverter, max continuous output 0.915 kW. CEC weighted efficiency averages efficiencies measured at several load points under the CEC/Sandia test protocol. The list shows no last-updated date. The row is identical to APsystems' DS3-LV {120V} (0.915 kW, 95%). The datasheet claims 96% peak.

findings.note: The list holds 2,208 records. Sorting by nominal voltage ascending puts all 120 V rows at the top, and I read all 22 of them. This is an absence on one state list, not a measurement.

findings.label: Measured daily generation, Mighty Gadget (James Smythe)
findings.value: 2.12, 3.85, 2.32 and 3.35 kWh/day (20–23 June 2026); 14.7 kWh total for June
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Stream Microinverter Review - Affordable plug in solar to cover base load and reduce electricity bills - Mighty Gadget
findings.note: Review dated 2026-06-25. UK 800 W unit, not the US 1,200 W model. Two 460 W JA Solar panels leaned against a wall in a broadly north-facing, partly shaded garden during a heatwave. Shows real yield from a poor siting, not inverter efficiency. The review reports no standby draw and no peak watts.

unsourced: An independent bench or lab measurement (efficiency curve, night/standby draw, measured peak AC output) of any US 120 V plug-in inverter from a named reviewer such as RTINGS, Notebookcheck, c't, CNET or Stiftung Warentest. Searches turned up only maker specs, retailer copy and forum posts. chargedreviews.com/inverters/apsystems-ez1-lv says it does no independent testing.
A measured night tare (standby draw) for the EZ1-LV, HiFlow Pro LV or BDM-1200-LV. The CEC table I read has no night-tare column, and the EZ1-LV's 20 mW figure is only a maker datasheet claim.

Stiftung Warentest or c't measured efficiencies for the EU EZ1-M or HMS-800W-2T. Search showed only the test.de overview (bifacial 800 W kits) and no numbers. I did not open the paywalled reports, and they cover EU 230 V hardware anyway.
CEC weighted efficiency for the Hoymiles HMS-450-1WM-LV and HMS-500-1WM-LV, which were not among the 120 V rows on the CEC list.
Enphase IQ8M: its CEC entries are 240 V/208 V rooftop units. I did not pull its row because it is not a plug-in product.
